/-!
# Erdős Problem 645

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/645](https://www.erdosproblems.com/645)
- [BrLa99] Brown, Tom C. and Landman, Bruce M., Monochromatic arithmetic progressions with large
  differences. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1999), 21--35.
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace Erdos645

/--
If ℕ is $2$-coloured then there must exist a monochromatic three-term arithmetic progression
$x,x+d,x+2d$ such that $d>x$.

This was first proved by Brown and Landman [BrLa99], who in fact show that this is always possible
with $d>f(x)$ for any increasing function $f$.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and ChatGPT.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos645.lean"]
theorem erdos_645 (c : ℕ → Bool) : ∃ x d, 0 < x ∧ x < d ∧
    (∃ C, c x = C ∧ c (x + d) = C ∧ c (x + 2 * d) = C) := by
  sorry

end Erdos645

review.notes: The sole declaration has the correct quantifier order, two-colour domain, positive initial term, strict large-difference condition, and monochromaticity condition. Brown–Landman define their progressions on positive integers with d ≥ f(x); taking f(x) = x + 1 gives the displayed claim. Their arbitrary-function theorem also supports the docstring's d > f(x) remark by increasing the threshold. Scratch Lean proofs checked the common-colour and positive-integer-witness equivalences, ruled out degenerate triples, and tested constant and nonconstant colourings. The linked external theorem has exactly the repository statement and contains no proof placeholders. After two tactic-only compatibility edits for the available Lean version, its axioms were [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The primary paper and companion status database support the recorded solved/formal-proof status.
